title: To the land of a just king
hookLine: the Prophet ﷺ sends some to Abyssinia, where a king rules who wrongs no one (sirah)

cards: A leader who can't protect his people has a hard choice. He can tell them to hold on. He can tell them to fight.

Or he can tell them to leave. Ibn Ishaq says that when the Prophet, peace be upon him, saw what his companions were suffering, and that he could not shield them, he pointed them across the sea, to Abyssinia.
Not because the land was Muslim; it wasn't. Because of the man who ruled it. Today: hijrah.

teach.b: Here is what Ibn Ishaq has him say, in paraphrase: if you go to Abyssinia, you'll find a king there under whom no one is wronged. It is a land of truthfulness, until God makes a way out for you from what you're in.
Look at what he praises. Not the king's religion; he is a Christian, ruling a Christian land. Not his wealth or his army.
Justice. The Prophet trusted his people to a ruler of another faith because that ruler was fair. So some of the Muslims went.
Ibn Ishaq calls it the first emigration in Islam, the first hijrah, before the later one to Medina.
Among those who went, he names Uthman ibn Affan and his wife Ruqayyah, the Prophet's own daughter. This wasn't sending strangers away. He sent his child.
Umm Salamah, who went too, later remembered what they found.

teach.h: SAFE IN THEIR FAITH, FAR FROM HOME.
teach.b: In her report in Musnad Ahmad, she says they came to the best of neighbors, were safe in their faith, and worshipped God without being harmed or hearing anything they hated. Safe in their faith, in someone else's country.
Tomorrow, Quraysh come after them. For now, notice the picture: the first hijrah was Muslims running for safety to the court of a just king.

how: Muslims know this as the emigration to Abyssinia (al-Habashah), told in sirah lessons as the community's first hijrah, and the Negus is remembered with honor for sheltering them.

games.q: your people are being tortured and you can't protect them. what do you tell them?
o: go to a land where a just king rules, even of another faith.
hide and wait for it to pass.
games.why: Ibn Ishaq says the Prophet sent some to Abyssinia, where a king ruled under whom no one was wronged.

practice: Think of fairness from someone who owed you nothing: a person outside your circle, of another faith or background, who held the rules level when tilting them would have been easy, like an honest official, a referee who called it straight against the home crowd, a landlord who gave back the whole deposit.
Notice exactly what they did, and what it might have cost them. Then say your thanks quietly, naming the fair thing, and if you pray, you can pray for them.

wordCard.voice: Hijrah. The Prophet sends companions to Abyssinia, the first emigration in Islam, to a king who, he says, rules so that no one is wronged. Today's word.

orig.note: Arabic: emigration, leaving one place for another; Ibn Ishaq calls the journey to Abyssinia the first hijrah in Islam.

carryVoice: Your line: a just king. Justice, not religion, was the reason he gave. That's day seven hundred forty-two.

sources.ref: Ibn Ishaq, Sirat Rasul Allah (the first emigration to Abyssinia: a king under whom none is wronged, a land of truthfulness; Uthman and Ruqayyah among the emigrants)
